terms.grammar: verb, irregular, conjugated like eō: the passive of vēndō
evidence: Vulg. Mt. 10.29: duo passerēs asse vēneunt
terms.comment: “Be sold” is not a passive of vēndō, which classical prose does not use apart from the participles vēnditus, vēndendus (Lewis & Short), but vēneō, “go to sale”: vēneunt, they are sold; vēnībunt, they will be sold; vēnīsse, to have been sold.

phrases.english: How much are you selling this for?
Aren’t two sparrows sold for a penny?

phrases.latin: vēnībunt servī, supellex, fundī, aedēs, omnia. vēnībunt quīquī licēbunt, praesentī pecūniā.
phrases.english: For sale: slaves, furniture, farms, house, everything. They will be sold for whatever they fetch, cash down.

phrases.latin: eum forte agrum in quō ipse castra habēret vēnīsse nihil ob id dēminūtō pretiō
phrases.english: that the very field he was camped on had been sold, at no lower price for that

phrases.latin: surgite: jam vēndit puerīs jentācula pistor
phrases.english: get up: the baker is already selling the boys their breakfast
